geographic_scope_summary: STRUCTURED_STATUS: only the geometry (443 GMS polygons, IDs, parity, provenance) is certified structured data; Yukon has NO certified rule bundle, so species-GMS relationships, season dates, bag limits, PHA/threshold areas and special-area restrictions exist only as research notes and the quoted authority text. Authority scope: big game seasons/bag limits are written per Game Management Subzone (GMS, 443 in 11 Game Management Zones (GMZ)), each species row lists its own GMS ranges (e.g. male moose Zone 1: 1-04, 1-05, 1-12 to 1-15, 1-17 to 1-19, 1-21 to 1-72). Small game and non-migratory game birds are territory-wide with Zone 6 + GMS 4-03 closed (Zone 5 sharp-tailed grouse limit differs). Overlays: national parks/sanctuaries closed (Ivvavik, Kluane, Vuntut, Herschel Island-Qikiqtaruk, Kluane Wildlife Sanctuary, Ddhaw Ghro HPA), two 800 m roadway corridors, Dempster corridor (8 km) vehicle rules, partial-subzone areas (portion of 5-21, sub-areas of 8-24 to 8-27, 'portion of' 3-02, 5-06, 1-25, 1-28, 5-06), PHA lottery areas (Schedule C), threshold/registration hunts (Faro, Mayo, Fortymile, Nelchina), time-limited closures (GMS 5-17 sheep to 2026-10-31; five south-Dempster subzones closed to caribou after Oct 31), First Nation Settlement Land consent rules (map-based, separate legal context). Bag limits are territory-wide, not per zone. Migratory birds: federal.

geographic_scope_summary: Connecticut is a town-based system. Deer and turkey: 13 numbered private-land Deer/Turkey Management Zones (1,2,3,4A,4B,5-12), published only as a map made of whole towns; zones change only private-land bag limits (zones 2 and 4A no antlerless-only tag; zone 7 +1 antlerless; zones 11 and 12 +2 antlerless, a January 31 archery extension and replacement tags) and the baiting ban (zones 1-10 all land, zones 11-12 state land only); all other deer/turkey season dates are statewide, qualified by LAND STATUS (private land vs state land vs named state-land parcels, lottery areas, bowhunting-only areas), not by zone. State land is itemised by named parcel (guide tables pp.47-58; DEEP layer of 178 areas). Waterfowl: North/South Zone split at Interstate 95 (text), plus three Canada goose units AP/AFRP/NAP-H defined by county, town lists and highway lines (text and a 169-town table with 18 split towns described by road). Other species (small game, pheasant, bear etc.) not decomposed here: guide seasons appear statewide with land-status qualifiers. Sunday hunting is a land-status/implement overlay (private land only; migratory birds never).

(1) Game Management Unit 1 consists of all mainland drainages from Dixon Entrance to Cape Fairweather, those islands east of the center line of Clarence Strait from Dixon Entrance to Caamano Point, all islands in Stephens Passage and Lynn Canal north of Taku Inlet, Pleasant Island, and all seaward waters and lands within three miles of these coastlines; (A) Unit 1(A) consists of all drainages in Unit 1 south of the latitude of Lemesurier Point including all drainages into Behm Canal and excluding all drainages of Ernest Sound; (B) Unit 1(B) consists of all drainages in Unit 1 between the latitude of Lemesurier Point and the latitude of Cape Fanshaw, including all drainages of Ernest Sound and Farragut Bay, and including the islands east of the center lines of Frederick Sound, Dry Strait (between Sergief and Kadin Islands), Eastern Passage, Blake Channel (excluding Blake Island), Ernest Sound and Seward Passage; (C) Unit 1(C) consists of that portion of Unit 1 draining into Stephens Passage and Lynn Canal north of Cape Fanshaw and south of the latitude of Eldred Rock, including Berner's Bay, and Sullivan Island, and that portion north of Icy Strait and south of the latitude of Eldred Rock, including Pleasant Island, and excluding drainages into Farragut Bay; (D) Unit 1(D) consists of that portion of Unit 1 north of the latitude of Eldred Rock, excluding Sullivan Island and the drainages of Berners Bay; (2) Game Management Unit 2 consists of Prince of Wales Island and all islands west of the center lines of Clarence Strait and Kashevarof Passage, south and east of the center lines of Sumner Strait, and east of the longitude of the westernmost point on Warren Island, and all seaward waters and lands within three miles of these coastlines; (3) Game Management Unit 3 consists of all islands west of Unit 1(B), north of Unit 2, south of the center line of Frederick Sound, and east of the center line of Chatham Strait, including Coronation, Kuiu, Kupreanof, Mitkof, Zarembo, Kashevarof, Woronkofski, Etolin, Wrangell, and Deer Islands, and all seaward waters and lands within three miles of these coastlines; (4) Game Management Unit 4 consists of all islands south and west of Unit 1(C) and north of Unit 3, including Admiralty, Baranof, Chichagof, Yakobi, Inian, and Lemesurier Islands, and all seaward waters and lands within three miles of these coastlines; (5) Game Management Unit 5 consists of all Gulf of Alaska drainages and islands between Cape Fairweather and the center line of Icy Bay, including the Guyot Hills, and all seaward waters and lands within three miles of these coastlines; (A) Unit 5(A) consists of all drainages in Unit 5 east of Yakutat Bay, Disenchantment Bay, and the eastern edge of Hubbard Glacier, and includes the islands of Yakutat and Disenchantment Bays; (B) Unit 5(B) consists of the remainder of Unit 5; (6) Game Management Unit 6 consists of all Gulf of Alaska and Prince William Sound drainages from the center line of Icy Bay (excluding the Guyot Hills) to Cape Fairfield, including Kayak, Hinchinbrook, Montague, and adjacent islands, and Middleton Island, and all seaward waters and lands within three miles of these coastlines, but excluding the Copper River drainage upstream from Miles Glacier and those drainages on the north side of Miles Glacier, and excluding the Nellie Juan and Kings River drainages; (A) Unit 6(A) consists of Gulf of Alaska drainages in Unit 6 east of Palm Point near Katalla, including Kanak, Wingham, and Kayak Islands; (B) Unit 6(B) consists of Gulf of Alaska and Copper River Basin drainages in Unit 6 west of Palm Point near Katalla, east of the west bank of the Copper River, and east of a line from Flag Point to Cottonwood Point; (C) Unit 6(C) consists of drainages in Unit 6 west of the west bank of the Copper River, and west of a line from Flag Point to Cottonwood Point, and drainages east of the east bank of Rude River and drainages into the eastern shore of Nelson Bay and Orca Inlet; (D) Unit 6(D) consists of the remainder of Unit 6; (7) Game Management Unit 7 consists of Gulf of Alaska drainages between Gore Point and Cape Fairfield, including the Nellie Juan and Kings River drainages, the Kenai River drainages upstream of a line from the mouth of the Russian River, continuing southerly along the Chugach National Forest boundary to the upper end of Upper Russian Lake; and including the drainages into Upper Russian Lake east of the Chugach National Forest boundary, the drainages into the south side of Turnagain Arm west of and including the Portage Creek drainage, and east of 150 W. Long., and all Kenai Peninsula drainages east of 150 W. long., from Turnagain Arm to the Kenai River, and all seaward waters and lands within three miles of these coastlines; (8) Game Management Unit 8 consists of all islands southeast of the center line of Shelikof Strait, including Kodiak, Afognak, Whale, Raspberry, Shuyak, Spruce, Marmot, Sitkalidak, Amook, Uganik, and Chirikof Islands, the Trinity Islands, the Semidi Islands, and other adjacent islands, and all seaward waters and lands within three miles of these coastlines; (9) Game Management Unit 9 consists of the Alaska Peninsula and adjacent islands, including drainages east of False Pass, Pacific Ocean drainages west of and excluding the Redoubt Creek drainage, drainages into the south side of Bristol Bay, drainages into the north side of Bristol Bay east of Etolin Point, and including the Sanak and Shumagin Islands, and all seaward waters and lands within three miles of these coastlines; (B) Unit 9(B) consists of that portion of Unit 9 in the Kvichak River drainage, except those lands drained by the Kvichak River and Kvichak Bay between the Alagnak River drainage and the Naknek River drainage; geographic_scope_summary: Rules scoped by 26 Game Management Units, subdivided into lettered subunits (73 polygons incl. 10 undivided Z units), defined verbally by drainages, strait centre lines and latitudes; five regions; migratory birds by five zones defined as unit lists; state closed areas/refuges per unit; federal public lands overlay (parks closed; federal subsistence regs by same units).
pattern_reason: Authority text defines 26 units/subunits; agency MapServer has 73 matching subunit polygons (set equality with the lettered subunits in 5 AAC 92.450); migratory zones are unit lists.
suggested_strategy: AUTHORITY_GEOMETRY (ADF&G-hosted GMUSubunits MapServer, display use with attribution; consent needed to store/redistribute) + NON_POLYGON_RESOLVER for migratory-bird zones (unit -> zone lookup from the unit lists)
defining_language_quote: 5 AAC 92.450: "(1) Game Management Unit 1 consists of all mainland drainages from Dixon Entrance to Cape Fairweather, those islands east of the center line of Clarence Strait from Dixon Entrance to Caamano Point, all islands in Stephens Passage and Lynn Canal north of Taku Inlet, Pleasant Island, and all seaward waters and lands within three miles of these coastlines;"
gis_contents_verified: Layers 0,3,4 count 73; fields Region, UnitSub (e.g. 01A, 02Z), SubLabel, SubLetter, SqMi, Shape_*; layer 2 count 5 regions. Lettered subunits in 5 AAC 92.450 text == lettered subunits in layer (empty set difference both ways); 10 Z units = undivided units.
gis_matches_legal_scope: YES for GMU/subunit scope (one polygon per subunit). NO polygons for migratory zones (derived from unit lists), state closed areas, refuges or federal land status. Agency states boundaries are not survey/GPS quality. Shapefile item is labelled eff 7/1/2025 vs 2026-27 regs.

geographic_scope_summary: Big-game/turkey/crane rules are scoped by county composition: 6 Deer Management Units (whole-county lists, all 95 counties), 5 Turkey Management Units (whole-county lists, all 95 counties), 6 Bear Hunt Zones (BHZ 1-5 + Transitional) built from whole counties plus counties split at named highways/interstates (I-40, Hwy 411, I-75, Old Lake City Hwy, Dutch Valley Rd, Hwy 63, Hwy 25E, Hwy 111), 10 Elk Hunt Zones that exist only inside North Cumberland WMA (textual road/ridge/creek descriptions) plus 5 designated private-land counties, and 2 sandhill crane zones (Southeast Crane Zone = south of I-40 and east of SR 56). Statewide spring turkey season dates/bag are uniform; fall turkey shotgun season is closed in named counties.
